answer: A bidder is admitted only after it fences one surveyed meadow strip for an entire season, presses a single violet from a GPS-locked row, and matches that flower's pollen to a relic seed-head taken from the same strip the year before and then incinerated. The strip cannot be subdivided mid-season, and the destroyed relic cannot be reused. A sybil operator would have to lease a thousand real strips and burn a thousand archive heads, so the land and specimen cost of faking a majority outruns any profit from bid-rigging.
